newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Kiguel welcomes IBCA BB rating.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Kiguel welcomes IBCA BB rating.

text.p: Argentina's Undersecretary of Finance Miguel Kiguel hailed European credit agency IBCA's decision Thursday to assign Argentina a BB rating with a "positive" outlook.
"This rating has the advantage of having a positive outlook. This indicates that IBCA has a more positive view than the other rating agencies," Kiguel told journalists.
IBCA gave a BB rating to Argentina's medium- and long-term foreign currency debt and a B rating to its short-term foreign debt, adding a "positive" outlook to the rating.
"This confirms the majority view that Argentina is a BB at the moment, but it gives more favorable perspectives for the future," he told reporters.
Standard & Poor's and Duff & Phelp's both also rate Argentine foreign currency debt BB, while Moody's puts it further away from an investment grade at its B1 rating.
Kiguel added that if Argentina continued with current economic policies, in "two or three years" the country could attain an investment-grade credit rating.

The official said he did not think the rating would have an immediate impact on the cost of financing, since the real difference to those costs would come when the country passed from speculative to investment grade.
The IBCA rating was seen having a "positive impact" in Europe because of the agency's influence there, said Kiguel.
